Review of Scrum map completeness
Discussion on common misunderstandings
Final questions and answers

seeded_failure.symptom: The team template shows Sprint Backlog items progressing without a Sprint Goal, and Daily Scrum ownership is assigned to the Product Owner.
seeded_failure.cause: The lab environment board template was created with the Sprint Goal commitment missing and Daily Scrum accountability reassigned.
seeded_failure.fix: Re-establish the Sprint Goal as the commitment for the Sprint Backlog and reassign Daily Scrum ownership to the Developers.

quiz: What three pillars form the foundation of empirical Scrum theory?
What are the maximum allowed time-boxes for Sprint Planning, Daily Scrum, Sprint Review, and Sprint Retrospective in a one-month sprint?
Which Scrum accountability is solely responsible for managing the Product Backlog?
What is the specific commitment associated with the Sprint Backlog artefact?
Who is responsible for inspecting progress toward the Sprint Goal during the Daily Scrum?
Can the Sprint Goal be changed during an active Sprint?
What must be met before an Increment can be considered complete?
lab_rubric: Scrum Map Completeness
Map visually represents all roles, events, artefacts, commitments, and time-boxes with clear visual relationships and zero missing elements
Map includes all mandatory roles, events, artefacts, and commitments described in the Scrum Guide
Map is missing 1 to 2 key elements such as commitments or official time-boxes
Map is incomplete or fundamental Scrum concepts are missing
Scenario Accuracy
Answers 19 to 20 scenario questions correctly with exact Scrum Guide references and rationale
Answers at least 16 out of 20 scenario questions correctly
Answers 12 to 15 scenario questions correctly
Answers fewer than 12 scenario questions correctly
Anti-pattern Identification
Correctly identifies underlying Scrum misunderstandings and provides actionable, Scrum Guide-compliant remedies
Identifies major anti-patterns in the scenarios accurately
Identifies symptoms of anti-patterns but misapplies Scrum Guide principles for fixes
Fails to recognize basic Scrum anti-patterns
Troubleshooting Seeded Failure
Identifies both the missing commitment and incorrect accountability independently and fixes them within 15 minutes
Correctly identifies and fixes the seeded template failures with minimal trainer assistance
Identifies the symptom but requires direct guidance to restore Scrum compliance
Unable to locate or correct the seeded framework errors
